title: Annual child-care routes differ across stable SNAP states while adjacent transition cells are too sparse
source_unit: identified SIPP person with November-to-December SNAP state and December-attached annual reference-year child-care fields

observations.period: 2024; SNAP no -> no; annual paid child care

denominator.unit: valid reference-parent person pairs with numeric/valid EPAY field

observations.method: Fay-BRR weighted descriptive November-to-December SNAP stable-state context using December annual EPAY; WPFINWGT from November and REPWGT1–REPWGT240.
observations.uncertainty: EPAY describes the fall reference-year child-care universe and is attached to a stable monthly SNAP pair; it is not a monthly care outcome or causal SNAP estimate.
observations.subgroup: Reference-parent persons with no SNAP in both November and December and valid annual paid-care status.
observations.counterinterpretation: Paid-care use can reflect resources, provider availability, work schedule, family care, and child composition; lower paid care is not lower care need.

observations.period: 2024; SNAP no -> no; annual child-care assistance

denominator.unit: valid reference-parent person pairs with numeric/valid EPAYHELP field

observations.method: Same Fay-BRR stable-state context method using December annual EPAYHELP.
observations.uncertainty: Annual assistance status is not a monthly benefit route, adequacy, or receipt spell and is not comparable to SNAP receipt as a program effect.
observations.subgroup: Reference-parent persons with no SNAP in both November and December and valid annual assistance status.
observations.counterinterpretation: Assistance may be conditional on care arrangements, eligibility, provider costs, or reporting and cannot be read as a complete support measure.

observations.period: 2024; SNAP no -> no; annual care prevented work

denominator.unit: valid reference-parent person pairs with valid EWORKMORE field

observations.method: Same Fay-BRR stable-state context method using December annual EWORKMORE.
observations.uncertainty: EWORKMORE describes whether fall child-care arrangements prevented work or working more; it is not monthly time loss and is conditional on the reference-parent care universe.
observations.subgroup: Reference-parent persons with no SNAP in both November and December and valid annual work-prevention status.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported work prevention can reflect schedules, provider routes, costs, family alternatives, or labor demand; it is not a SNAP effect.

observations.period: 2024; SNAP yes -> yes; annual paid child care

denominator.unit: valid reference-parent person pairs with numeric/valid EPAY field

observations.method: Fay-BRR weighted descriptive November-to-December SNAP stable-state context using December annual EPAY.
observations.uncertainty: Small stable-SNAP care universe; annual paid-care status is not a monthly care outcome or causal SNAP estimate.
observations.subgroup: Reference-parent persons with SNAP in both November and December and valid annual paid-care status.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower paid care may indicate unpaid/family care, different work or child composition, provider constraints, or reporting rather than lower need.

observations.period: 2024; SNAP yes -> yes; annual child-care assistance

denominator.unit: valid reference-parent person pairs with numeric/valid EPAYHELP field

observations.method: Same Fay-BRR stable-state context method using December annual EPAYHELP.
observations.uncertainty: Small stable-SNAP care universe; annual assistance status is not a SNAP amount, monthly benefit route, or causal effect.
observations.subgroup: Reference-parent persons with SNAP in both November and December and valid annual assistance status.
observations.counterinterpretation: The higher assistance share can reflect care-need, eligibility, provider, or composition differences rather than SNAP causing childcare assistance.

observations.period: 2024; SNAP yes -> yes; annual care prevented work

denominator.unit: valid reference-parent person pairs with valid EWORKMORE field

observations.method: Same Fay-BRR stable-state context method using December annual EWORKMORE.
observations.uncertainty: Small stable-SNAP care universe; EWORKMORE describes annual fall child-care work prevention and is not monthly time loss or a causal SNAP outcome.
observations.subgroup: Reference-parent persons with SNAP in both November and December and valid annual work-prevention status.
observations.counterinterpretation: The difference may reflect selection into stable receipt, household composition, care need, work conditions, or reporting; it does not show SNAP caused work prevention.

related_sources.claim: The audit preserves the complete v16 slice, replicate archive, transition-pair counts, and sparse-transition warning.

boundary: This record compares annual/reference-year child-care fields among people observed in stable November-to-December SNAP states. It does not estimate SNAP effects, monthly care change, benefit adequacy, hours lost, notice, effort, remedy, or political response. The adjacent no-to-yes and yes-to-no transition cells are too sparse for promoted population estimates.
